exposure: Mode of delivery (prelabor cesarean section vs. non-instrumental vaginal delivery)
outcome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes (assessed using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire, second edition (ASQ-II))
cohort: Infants born by prelabor cesarean section compared to infants born by non-instrumental vaginal delivery
finding: Infants born by prelabor cesarean section had significantly lower ASQ-II scores in all domains at 4 months of age, and lower gross motor scores at 12 months of age, compared to infants born vaginally.
mod_finding: Infants born by prelabor cesarean section had significantly lower neurodevelopmental scores at 4 and 12 months of age compared to infants born vaginally.
